notes: SISTER-BRAND INDEPENDENCE CHECK (per brief note): AllModern runs on the same Wayfair Inc. platform/tech stack as Wayfair (S.N.1/c1.json), Birch Lane and Joss & Main (both linked from AllModern's own header via handover.php store-swap links: from_store=81 [AllModern] to_store=49 [Wayfair], 422 [Birch Lane], 450 [Joss & Main], 457 [Perigold]), but the catalog is genuinely independent: distinct category-ID namespace (e.g. Chandeliers is c477071 on AllModern vs c215419 on Wayfair) and wildly different per-category counts (Chandeliers 221 on AllModern vs 49678 on Wayfair; Wall Mirrors 260 vs Wayfair's 65928) -- confirms separate storefront inventory, not a mirrored catalog, same discipline as the Momax/XXXLutz precedent. Treated as a fully independent extraction, not a duplicate-company case. ACCESS: allmodern.com's homepage and robots.txt are reachable via plain direct fetch (HTTP 200, no bot-specific Disallow rules -- only a generic User-agent:* policy that explicitly Allows /*/sb0/ listing paths, which is what all leaf URLs here use). Category/listing pages (both /cat/ hub pages and /sb0/ listing pages) return HTTP 429 PerimeterX captcha ('Access to this page has been denied', px-captcha) to a plain requests session, but succeed reliably via curl_cffi browser impersonation (profile chrome131 or safari17_0; chrome124/chrome120/edge101 stayed blocked) with no IP pinning needed (ordinary IPv4 route works, unlike wayfair.com). qty is the listing grid's resultCount from the page's embedded React tracking-metadata JSON (data-tracking-metadata resultCount / BlockBuilderBrowseResultCount block), the same evidence field used for Wayfair (c1.json); a single consistent value was found per URL, no averaging/estimation. Full taxonomy was recovered from AllModern's own site-wide mega-nav (a static component present identically on every page, ~260-345 links), so no per-page sub-nav crawling was needed beyond confirming a handful of ambiguous 'cat' nodes were themselves childless leaf listings (Decorative Trays/Plates/Bowls, Decorative Objects, Creamers + Shakers all have their own direct resultCount and no further nav children). CROSS-CHECK: Outdoor Lighting's hub page resultCount (199) exactly equals the sum of its 4 child leaves (130+8+25+36=199), and Mirrors' All Mirrors total (299) exactly equals Floor+Full Length Mirrors (39) + Wall Mirrors (260); both confirm the resultCount field is a reliable exact aggregate, not inflated -- so hub/aggregate nodes were kept as parent rows (qty null) rather than double-counted as extra leaves. FACET-RECUT EXCLUSIONS (Rule 0.6): under Wall Art, Photography (138) + Paintings (192) + Abstract Art (784) + Oversized Wall Art (600) sum to far more than the All Wall Art total (1032), proving these are overlapping style/subject/size facets of the same pool (a piece can be both 'Abstract' and 'Oversized'), not disjoint catalog nodes -- dropped per 'facet re-cuts: compare product-ID sets, not names'; Wall Art Sets (114, a bundling facet) dropped for the same reason. Kept Framed Wall Art (620) + Canvas Wall Art (230) alongside All Wall Art (1032) since medium-type (framed vs canvas) is a materially distinct catalog split, matching the same Framed/Canvas Art split already established as genuine on sibling Wayfair (c1.json). MIXED ROLL-UP: Candles (sb0 resultCount 122) mixes scented products (e.g. 'Terra Tabac Scented Jar Candle', 'Hinoki Sage Scented Jar Candle', 'Citronella Pillar Candle') with unscented ones (e.g. 'Beautifully Done Unscented Taper Candle Set') under one listing node; the page exposes a 'Scented / Unscented' filter facet in its embedded JSON but with no per-option counts and no discoverable static filter-URL pattern to isolate an exact unscented-only total -- left qty null + MANUAL REVIEW per the brief's scented-candle exclusion and 'drop, don't pad' rule rather than reporting the mixed total or guessing a split. EXCLUDED (checked and deliberately dropped, not overlooked): Ceiling Fans and Light Bulbs (explicit brief exclusions); Wallpaper; Curtains + Drapes; Floor + Wall Tile (building material, not decor); Decorative Baskets + Boxes (111 -- sample titles dominated by 'Storage Basket'/'Storage Bin'/'Rattan Basket', i.e. functional storage, not decorative boxes); Organizational Decor (408 -- sample titles 'Tiered Shelf', 'Floating Shelf', 'Storage Bin', functional organization/shelving, not decor); Wall Shelves, Jewelry Organizers, Pet Accessories, Tabletop Games; a second/legacy 'Decorative Objects & Sculptures' URL (c1875408, resultCount 108) that partially overlaps the canonical Decorative Objects node (c1861442, resultCount 131, canonical of the same nav link) -- only the canonical node was kept to avoid double-counting; Coat Racks + Hooks (filed by the site itself under Furniture, not Decor); all Furniture, Rugs, Bedding, Storage, Baby+Kids, Pillows/Throws/Blankets/Poufs (textiles); Faux Flowers, Faux Plants + Trees (explicit faux-plant exclusion) and Live Plants + Trees (living plants are not a decor accessory; only containers/planters would qualify and AllModern's only Planters node is filed under Outdoor Furniture/Patio Decor, not Home Decor, and reads as an outdoor-living/patio item rather than an indoor decorative planter line, so it was left out; flagged here for visibility rather than silently dropped); Flatware Sets, Serving Utensils, Bar + Wine Tools (cutlery/tools, excluded per brief); Table Cloths + Runners, Napkins/Placemats/Chargers (bundled with textiles, mixed roll-up dropped whole since no separate charger-only node exists), Kitchen Towels; Stovetop/Electric Tea Kettles, Coffee Makers (small appliances); Kitchen/Bathroom Fixtures + Hardware, Sinks/Faucets, Tubs, Toilets, Shower doors/heads, Cabinet Knobs + Pulls (hardware/plumbing); Bath Mats/Towels/Linens/Shower Curtains/Trash Cans/Vanities/Medicine Cabinets/Bathroom Storage (bath furniture/storage/fixtures, only Vanity Lighting and Vanity Mirrors were kept from the Bath department per the mirrors/lighting carve-out); all 'Shop All'/'New'/'Sale'/'Best Sellers'/'Collections'/'Inspiration'/curated marketing pages (deals-and-design-ideas 'shop by room/style' pages) were never treated as taxonomy nodes.
